있지만 급격히 무너지지는 않고 있다. 이 밖에도 주택가격의 선행지표인 주택재고 및 공실률의 경우에도 최근 상승하고 있지만 
우려할 수준은 아니다. 주택재고 부담 등으로 주택가격이 당장 급락하지는 않을 것이다.

미국 투자사이클과 고용시장도 주택시장 둔화의 방어막 역할 
모기지 금리 추가 급등 시 주택시장의 악영향을 피하기는 어려울 수 있다. 그러나, 이전에 비해 가계 등 경제 전반에 금리 충격을 
상쇄시켜줄 방어막이 있어 모기지 금리 급등에도 불구하고 주택시장이 단기적으로 큰 혼란에 빠질 여지는 크지 않다. 일단 미 
연준의 추가 금리인상이 현실화되고 있지만 기준금리 수준이 22년 금리인상 사이클 고점인 5.5% 수준까지 상승하지 않을 것이다. 
현재 국채금리 수준이 이미 미 연준의 추가 금리인상을 2~3차례 반영하고 있다는 점에서 미 연준의 추가 금리인상 폭이 확대되거나 
인플레이션 압력이 급격히 높아지지 않는다면 국채금리의 추가 상승여력은 제한적일 수 있다. 이는 모기지 금리의 추가 상승폭 역시 
제한적임을 의미한다. 
앞서도 잠시 언급했지만 그래도 고용시장이 기업들의 실적 호조 등으로 급격히 위축될 여지가 크지 않다는 점은 가계의 추가 금리 
부담을 방어해주는 역할을 할 것이다. 무엇보다 미국 투자 및 제조업 경기가 강한 모멘텀을 유지하고 있음은 이전 모기지 금리 급등 
당시와 차별되는 현상이다. 즉 미국내 강한 투자와 제조업 모멘텀이 미국 주택시장 불안 증폭을 낮추는 요인으로 작용할 것이다. 
요약하면 금리 급등과 고금리 현상 장기화는 경기 및 산업전반에 악영향을 미칠 수밖에 없고 주택시장은 고금리에 더더욱 취약한 
구조를 지니고 있다. 그러나 다행히 미국내 강한 투자와 제조업 모멘텀이 높은 모기지 금리에 따른 주택시장 침체 리스크를 당분간 
막아주는 역할을 할 것으로 기대한다. 다만, 고금리 수준이 내년 중반까지 지속된다면 주택시장 침체 리스크가 크게 부각될 위험은 
잠재해 있다.

### Page 1

2026-10-01 
Economy Brief

성장과 금리간 싸움 결과, 유가에 달렸다 Economy Brief 
[경제] 박상현 2122-9196 shpark@imfnsec.com

Check Point 
8월 PCE 물가지수만으로 미국 인플레이션 압력 둔화를 단정하기에는 어려움. 전년동월 기준 코어 PCE 물가는  
7월과 동일했고 8월 슈퍼 코어 PCE 물가 상승률은 7월대비 큰 폭 상승함   
성장 모멘텀이 강하다는 점은 긍정적임. 명목 GDP 성장률이 잠정치보다 0.5%p 상향된 전기비연울 8.5%를 기록   
금리와 성장 그리고 물가간 치열한 싸움이 이어질 것으로 예상되는 가운데 승패의 핵심 변수는 유가임

다소 안도감을 준 물가와 강한 성장 모멘텀   
물가와 성장관련 지표가 시장 예상과는 다소 엇갈렸다. 8월 PCE 물가지수는 시장 예상치를 하회했다. 8월 PCE 물가지수는 전월비 
0.3%(전년동월 3.4%)로 시장 예상치에 부합했지만 코어 PCE 물가지수는 전월비 0.2%로 시장 예상치 0.3%를 소폭 하회했다. 
반면에 2분기 GDP 성장률은 잠정치인 전기비 연율 1.5%보다 개선된 전기비 연율 2.2%를 기록했다. 물가는 우려보다 안정적이었고 
강력한 성장 모멘텀이 GDP를 통해 확인되었다. 
다만, 8월 PCE 물가지수만으로 미국 인플레이션 압력 둔화를 단정하기에는 이른 감이 있다. 일단 코어 PCE 물가는 시장 예상치를 
하회했지만 전년동월 기준 PCE 물가 상승률은 7월과 동일했다. 더욱이 에너지와 임대료를 제외한 8월 슈퍼 코어 PCE 물가 
상승률은 7월대비 큰 폭 상승했다. 8월 슈퍼 코어 PCE 물가는 전월비 0.36%로 7월(0.07%)대비 큰 폭 상승했고 전년동월 
기준으로도 3.46%로 7월 3.42%대비 소폭 상승했다.  
또 하나 8월 코어 PCE 물가 상승률이 시장 예상치를 하회했음에도 불구하고 금융시장이 반색하지 못한 이유는 디젤유 가격 등 일부 
에너지 가격 상승분이 8월 수치에는 제대로 반영되지 않아 9월 PCE 물가 지표에 상승 압력으로 작용할 커졌기 때문이다. 실제로 
9월 월 평균 유가(WTI기준) 수준은 95.7달러로 8월 월 평균 유가(82.5달러) 대비 16% 급등했다. 따라서 9월 소비지물가 및 PCE 
물가 상승률이 전월대비 큰 폭으로 상승할 여지가 크다. 아직은 에너지발 인플레이션 압력을 안도하기 이른 시점이다.  
한편 성장 모멘텀이 강하다는 점은 긍정적이다. 2분기 GDP 성장률 확정치는 민간투자와 소비지출이 상향 조정된 영향으로 잠정치 
대비 0.7%p 상향 조정되었다. 실질 성장률과 함께 주목되는 명목 GDP 성장률 역시 잠정치(전기비연율 8.0%)보다 0.5%p 상향된 
8.5%를 기록했다. 명목 GDP 성장률 수준이 주목하는 이유는 아무래도 고금리 수준을 상회하는 명목 GDP 성장률이 미국 경제가 
고금리 충격을 방어 혹은 이겨내고 있음을 시사하기 때문이다. 명목 GDP 성장률 추이와 관련하여 주목되는 또 다른 흐름은 기업 
이익 추이다. <그림3>에서 보듯 비금융기관 기업이익 규모는 2분기 명목 GDP대비 9.8%로 1966년 이후 가장 높은 수준이다. 
고금리 환경 속에서도 기업 이익은 강한 모멘텀을 유지하고 있다.

금리와 성장간 줄다리기는 당분간 이어질 듯: 핵심은 유가   
8월 PCE 물가가 일부 안도감을 주었지만 미국 장기 국채금리는 또 다시 상승했다. 8월 PCE 물가만으로 인플레이션 리스크 완화 및 
10월 미 연준의 추가 금리인상 우려를 충분히 해소시키기에는 미흡했기 때문이다. 추후 발표되는 9월 소비자물가 결과가 더욱 
중요해졌다. 미 연준의 추가 금리인상 우려와 더불어 성장 모멘텀도 국채금리 추가 상승의 빌미를 제공했다. 2분기 GDP 성장률 상향 
조정과 함께 3분기 GDP 성장률은 2분기보다 더욱 높아질 수 있다는 기대감이 국채금리의 상승 요인으로 작용했다.

현상이지만 고금리 장기화 리스크를 무시하기 어렵다. 금리가 현 수준보다는 낮아질 필요가 있으며 그 촉매제는 성장둔화보다는 
물가, 즉 유가 안정에서 찾아야 한다. 10월에도 금리와 성장 그리고 물가간 치열한 싸움이 이어질 것으로 예상되는 가운데 승패의 
핵심 변수는 유가일 것이다.

The bank
for a changing
world
History tends to repeat itself in advanced economies. Once again, growth ultimately fell short of expectations by only a small
margin in the first half of 2026, despite the conflict in Iran. As early as 2025, the impact of tariffs was less severe than feared.
This is a sign that structural factors (notably AI, defence and electrification) are underpinning growth in these countries

and are expected to continue to do so in 2027. However, there are significant risks to the economic outlook, primarily of a
geopolitical nature, with a significant upside risk to inflation and interest rates. The other instance of history repeating itself
concerns a period that those under 20 cannot have experienced: the period leading up to the 2008 crisis, echoes of which can
be seen in terms of growth, inflation, the direction of monetary policy, and long-term interest rates.

Advanced economies are experiencing trends similar to those they
faced nearly 20 years ago:
- Growth remains resilient in 2025-26 despite shocks, as it did in 2006-
07, in the major advanced economies.
- Inflation is above central banks’ targets: as in 2006-07, this calls for a
tightening of monetary policy.
- In Europe and the United States, long-term interest rates have re -
turned to their 2006-07 levels (1996 in Japan): a challenging environ-

ment for public finances in a context where public debt ratios are signi-
ficantly higher than those seen 20 years ago.
THE GLOBAL ECONOMY IN THE MIDST OF A GROWTH CYCLE
We are already well into 2026, and the picture so far is clear: glo -
bal growth is proving resilient. Following a US tariff shock last year,
growth is once again proving, for the time being, to be significantly less
affected by the conflict in Iran than had been anticipated when it first

broke out. Initially, however, there were fears that this new shock would
hit growth even harder. As with the tariff hike in 2025, the impact was
measurable, particularly in terms of consumer confidence. But in both
2025 and 2026, growth has also shown a degree of resilience.
The figures for the second quarter bear this out, despite the sharp rise
in oil prices, the recessionary impact of which is not yet apparent.
According to our forecasts, growth was expected to reach or exceed 1%

in 2026 in the four major advanced economies (the Eurozone, Japan,
the United Kingdom and the United States, where it exceeds 2%) for
the second consecutive year. This had not happened (excluding the
post-COVID catch-up period) since 2006-07. Growth figures are more
moderate (particularly for demographic reasons), but the private sec -
tor is not (at present) showing the same excesses (at that time, the
credit boom had preceded the worst crisis since the 1930s); although

debt levels have recently risen in the US tech sector.
The driving force behind the current growth cycle is clear: artificial
intelligence (AI). It is fuelling global trade and business investment
in most countries. This is clearly the case in the United States, where
business investment is growing strongly as investment plans in the
US tech sector are implemented.
However, the world’s major economies are currently engaged in a
broader push to expand their capital goods investment. Alongside the

ongoing development of services—particularly digital services—we
have seen a rebound in industrial production in most countries since
early 2025. The leading sectors are primarily technology equipment,
machinery, aeronautics, defence and their essential inputs (energy and
metals). This trend is evident everywhere, including in Europe, and
is becoming entrenched over the long term, with an improvement in
business climate indicators, particularly new export orders. Growth is

therefore expected to strengthen further in 2027, particularly in the
Eurozone, where German investment plans are set to gather momen -
tum and whose spillover effects will have a greater impact on the eco-
nomy.
However, not all sectors are experiencing the same momentum. This
is particularly true for the sectors that depend on household consump-
tion, which has shown mixed trends. Our observation that consumer
spending is more buoyant in the United States than in Europe was

confirmed in 2026, and the outlook does not point to a change in this
ranking.
EDITORIAL
RESILIENCE TO SHOCK AFTER SHOCK

The bank
for a changing

While European and US households are experiencing more or less the
same energy price shock, inflation remains higher in the United States.
But this has not prevented consumer spending from keeping pace, pri-
marily because it is driven by the wealthiest households, who are less
sensitive to inflation than to the wealth effect. Furthermore, while the

savings rate remains high in the Eurozone, US households have been
drawing down their savings. This is also true of British households,
which explains why the UK has seen slightly stronger growth since
the beginning of the year. In Japan, government spending has partially
offset energy inflation (while other countries are doing so to a much
lesser extent than in 2022), which has supported consumption growth.
However, these buffers—reduced savings or fiscal support—have their

limits when shocks persist. The two major current conflicts (Iran and
Ukraine) are far from being resolved, and their impact is continuing.
This persistent geopolitical risk and its implications for inflation repre-
sent a significant headwind to the growth outlook for 2027.
HIGHER INFLATION CALLS FOR MONETARY TIGHTENING
Inflation is exceeding the target set by three of the four central banks
examined in this publication, which is another similarity (albeit with

different underlying causes) with the 2006-07 period. Japan is the ex -
ception, as government support measures for households are tempo -
rarily holding back inflation.
Apart from the Bank of Japan, which is engaged in a long-term norma-
lisation process, no central bank was expected to raise its key rates
in 2026. But they are now being prompted to do so for reasons that
vary from one region to another. The first is the conflict in Iran and
the resulting rise in oil prices, which triggered a rebound in energy

inflation from the second quarter onwards. However, since the conflict
was not resolved by the memorandum of understanding signed in June,
and given that the subsequent drop in oil prices proved short-lived,
inflation is expected to rise again. The rise in gas prices is expected to
exacerbate the impact, particularly in Europe, where inventories are
being replenished ahead of winter. Electricity prices are expected to
follow suit in most countries, but at a more moderate pace than in

2022. Indeed, gas is now used less to generate electricity than it was
at that time (thanks to the expansion of renewable energy), and to an
even lesser extent in France.
There is a significant risk that energy inflation will spread further to
other components of inflation in the future, and inflation expectations
could eventually reflect this. This is why the European Central Bank
has already raised its key interest rate twice (in June and September)

and, according to our scenario, will likely do so again in December. For
the same reason, we expect the Bank of England to raise its policy rate
in November. Although the cap on energy prices was maintained for
a long time, it has now been raised. As a result, inflation is expected
to rise between now and the end of the year. The aim will then be to
prevent second-round effects.
Inflation can also be a sign of (too much) economic strength. In the

United States, it has exceeded the 2% target since 2021. The main
argument in favour of a new cycle of rate hikes (following the one in
2022-2023) lies in the current resilience of growth and the improving
labour market. The Federal Reserve (Fed) must balance two equally
important objectives: maximum employment and price stability. Howe-
ver, unlike in the 4 th quarter of 2025, when the decline in job crea -
tion justified monetary easing (by 75 basis points), the current sharp

rebound in job creation completely reverses that analysis. According
to our forecasts, the unemployment rate is expected to decrease in
the coming months, which pushes back the prospect of a decline in
core inflation. This situation persists due to both supply constraints
(over which a central bank has no control) and excess demand (which
the Fed can, however, mitigate). Consequently, the Fed raised its key
rate in September and is expected to implement two further rate hikes

between now and January 2027.
In Japan, finally, while headline inflation has been brought down by
government support measures, core inflation remains significant.
Wage pressures are mounting against a backdrop of labour shortages.
The Bank of Japan is therefore being forced to accelerate the pace of its
monetary normalisation.
In all these regions, inflation is currently expected to peak in Q4 2026
or Q1 2027. It is against this backdrop of temporary inflation that rate

hikes could also come to an end by that time (excluding Japan). Howe-
ver, this assumes that once the energy shock—the course of which
remains uncertain—subsides, inflation will fall. The effects of El Niño,
which are still difficult to gauge at present, could take over. Inflation
would then remain above the central banks’ target for a longer period.
Under this scenario, rate hikes would go further than is currently en -
visaged.
THE RISE IN LONG- TERM INTEREST RATES: A FACTOR THAT WILL WEIGH

ON PUBLIC FINANCES
Monetary policies have also to offset the inflationary effects of fiscal
policy, particularly in the United States (where the budget deficit is
high and shows no signs of shrinking) and in Japan (where the new
government is pursuing pro-growth policies). In Europe, fiscal policy
is playing a much smaller role than it did in 2022. While the stimulus
measures implemented at that time did help reduce the inflation rate
in the short term (by nearly 2.5 pp in France, for example), by keeping

demand at a high level, they delayed disinflation and increased the
scale of the monetary tightening required.
The outbreak of the conflict in Iran acted as a catalyst: it triggered a
rise in long-term rates (which had been trending downwards at the
start of the year) to levels close to those of 2006-07. This rise is wides-
pread, but its causes vary. Inflation expectations appear to play a more
significant role in the Eurozone, whereas the rise in real interest rates

seems to be the main factor in the United States and Japan.

Higher inflation and more resilient real growth than feared point in
the same direction: stronger than expected nominal growth that is li -
kely to be sustained. However, in the long term, high nominal growth
tends to drive up nominal interest rates (as it is a positive sign of more
profitable investment projects), in contrast to the problem of secular

stagnation raised in the 2010s (which combined low nominal growth
with low nominal interest rates).
The other issue is the high level of fiscal deficits (too high for a period
of growth), with various situations. In several countries, the public
debt-to-GDP ratio continues to rise. In the United States, deficit reduc-
tion does not appear to be a priority, to the extent that it is expected
to remain above 6% of GDP at the very least until the end of Donald

Trump’s term of office (with little hope that the mid-term elections will
significantly alter this trend). In the United Kingdom and France, fiscal
consolidation has begun, but it is being hampered by the simultaneous
increase in certain areas of expenditure (debt servicing, defence and
healthcare, due in particular to an ageing population), which is slowing
the pace of consolidation. In Germany, the implementation of invest -
ment plans is leading to a widening of the deficit. While this does not

pose a sustainability problem, it does result in an increase in annual
debt issuance. In Japan, the budget deficit is kept in check by interest
payments that remain low, as the rise in interest rates is recent and
the average maturity of the debt is high (10 years). However, expansio-
nary fiscal policy could pose further problems in terms of debt dyna -
mics if it were to continue through the end of the decade. In Italy and
Spain, fiscal consolidation has been sufficient to stabilise the public

debt-to-GDP ratio (and even to reduce it in Spain), but the high level of
Italy’s debt service it vulnerable to a rise in interest rates.
In all these countries, the fiscal arithmetic is simpler today than it
will be in 2030. Indeed, in most cases, only half of the debt was is -
sued after 2022 (that is, after the end of the zero-interest-rate period).
The debt service has so far only partially risen, except in the United
States, where most of the increase has already occurred due to a shor-

ter average debt maturity (6 years). This means that, for all countries
combined, the rate of GDP growth remains higher than the average
interest rate paid on public debt (or the effective interest rate).
By 2030, the effective rate will have risen and caught up with
GDP growth. As a result, in most cases, the debt service will have re -
turned to the level as a share of GDP seen in the early 2000s. In order to
stabilise public debt-to-GDP ratios, primary balances will need to have

improved. This will even require the generation of primary surpluses,
particularly in Italy (which is already achieving this), France and the
United Kingdom. This is a crucial shift that governments will need to
introduce as early as the 2027 budget; otherwise, they risk postponing
the stabilisation of their public debt-to-GDP ratio once again.

SHIFT IN NARRATIVE

After a rough first half of the year, the 
narrative around Indonesia’s economy has 
turned relatively constructive . The macro 
outlook is on the mend, and policy coherence 
has strengthened. Recent budget 
developments have reduced the likelihood of an 
outright fiscal slippage. A more disciplined 
fiscal trajectory should also provide room for 
monetary policy to stay focused on its price 
stability mandate rather than on ad dressing 
financial stability risks due to fiscal concerns.

On the markets front, e ven as external triggers 
impacted the rupiah, the one -sided sharp 
depreciation run in the currency in the first half 
of the year has stalled . Debt markets have  
attracted offshore interest, alongside strong 
demand for shorter-tenor SRBI securities, all of 
which have contributed to the overall capital 
flows picture.

Ahead of MSCI’s final take on the domestic 
equity market’s classification in November, 
however, equity markets  find little favour . 
Nonetheless, material improvement s in the 
stock listing s and regulatory requirements 
undertaken by the stock market and financial 
regulators are expected to contribute to the 
medium-term stability of the capital markets.

Key domestic risks that plagued the economy 
in the first half of the year have been alleviated 
to some extent, while a few other monitorables 
remain.

NEAR-TERM FISCAL WORRIES 
RECEDE

Fiscal fears have moderated in the near 
term. New Finance Minister Suahasil 
Nazara reaffirmed the government’s 
commitment to maintain the annual 
deficit below -3% of GDP threshold. The 
2026 run-rate suggests that the deficit is 
likely to close within the budgeted target.

By September 2026, the fiscal deficit 
stood at 1.2% of GDP , reflecting a 
normalisation in spending and firm 
revenue growth. Total spending rose by 
a still -strong 1 9% yoy , even though the 
pace moderated from 1H, backed by 
disbursements towards the flagship free 
food program, subsidy and 
compensation outlays , as well as 
personnel expenditure.  Realised 
expenditure stood at 69% of the full -
year budget by 9M26.

On the other hand, revenues rose sharply 
by 25 .5% yoy (partly benefiting from 
base effects as readings were negative 
at the same time last year), helped by 
higher tax collections, export duties, and 
non-tax receipts. Revenues have already 
accounted for 74% of the budgeted 
scale by 9M26, suggesting full -year 
target is likely to be met.

Global crude prices are a key risk for the 
fiscal outlook, as prevailing Brent prices 
are above $100bl at the time of writing 
(vs budgeted ICP at $70bl), which will 
feed through higher subsidy and 
compensation outgoes, as authorities 
remain hesitant to raise fuel pump prices.

Significant efficiency measures have, 
however, been put in place  to contain 
spending, including reductions in 
outlays towards flagship schemes , 
which will help contain the extent of 
deterioration in the fiscal math. For 
instance, the flagship MBG program, 
which started with an allocation of IDR 
35trn, was  moderated to IDR 268trn 
(realised spending by Sep26 was IDR 
153trn). Successive stimulus packages

### Page 3

Indonesia: Policy mix aligns October 12, 2026 
                                                                                                                                            3

have been announced but the scale has 
been contained.

2027 math signals fiscal prudence, soft 
spots warrant attention

The official goalposts for 2027 point to 
a continued preference for fiscal 
prudence rather than fiscal activism.

Spending is on course to surpass the 
symbolic IDR 4000tn level, ris ing nearly 
4% yoy, with outlays divided between 
the centre and regional governments. 
The mix points to steady allocations 
towards subsidies, social transfers , and 
capital expenditure,  with ministry -level 
spending (K/L) set to contract, while non-
K/L spending is budgeted to increase. 
More notably, spending is expected to 
rise on key flagship programs – for 
instance, social protection (up 10%), the 
largest component education (up 14%) , 
which includes the free meals program 
at IDR 240trn.

On the revenue end, state revenues are 
expected to rise by 9% yoy compared to 
the budgeted 2026 APBN/ 7% vs the 
revised 2026 outlook. Compared to 
baseline 2026, tax revenues are 
expected to rise 10.5%, besides higher 
non-tax collections. This math lands the 
2027 budgeted deficit at -2.4% of GDP 
vs revised 2026 at -2.85% of GDP.

Few uncertainties that loom.  Firstly, 
next year’s math rests on an upbeat 
growth projection of 6 .0% (DBSf 5.2%) , 
besides modest depreciation in the 
rupiah and about  a 7% increase in the 
Indonesia crude price assumption (see 
table). Some of these expectations 
might be challenged as the year unfolds. 
Next, state revenues are expected to 
rise to a n upbeat  12.5% of GDP , likely 
riding on a strong growth forecast, 
better tax due diligence , and improved 
administration via the Coretax 
mechanism.

Thirdly, crude prices are a key risk to the 
fiscal math. Given the economy’s 
position as a net oil importer, various 
official commentaries put the sensitivity  
at every $1pb oil worsening the fiscal 
balance by IDR 6trn, after accounting for 
oil-related revenues. This implies that for 
every $10pb increase, the deficit could 
be impacted by ~IDR 60trn, not far from 
MOF’s sensitivity of IDR 68trn (~0.25 -
0.30% of GDP) due to higher subsidy and 
compensation costs  (ICT assumed at 
$75bl vs prevailing Brent at $100bl). 
Spending will need to reprioritised to 
accommodate additional allocation 
towards subsidies and compensation.

Next, the direction of travel on the

Discussions around the State Finance

Nonetheless, deficits/debt are likely to 
stay below key thresholds  and not 
emerge as a flashpoint for the markets.

MONETARY POLICY ON AN EVEN 
KEEL

Bank Indonesia has left the benchmark 
rate unchanged  since July 2026, after 
100bp hikes in 1H26. While tighter global 
financial conditions and geopolitical 
risks were key risks on the horizon, the BI 
held the domestic GDP forecast at 4.9 -
5.7% (DBSf: 5.3%) alongside 
manageable inflation, notwithstanding 
El Nino-related risks. Inflation rose to 3.3% 
yoy in Sep26, towards the high end of the 
target range. Authorities have, however, 
assured that the impact of higher food 
prices due to poor weather will be 
addressed through administrative 
measures by regional bodies.

Contained inflation expectations ha ve 
reduced the urgency for BI to tighten 
policy further, allowing policymakers to 
prioritise growth and financial stability 
considerations. The emphasis on 
strengthening the balance of payments 
position reflects continued caution over 
external financing conditions and capital 
flows. However, with the rupiah 
expected to remain stable on the back of 
policy measures and fundamenta ls, the 
BI did not view current external 
pressures as severe enough to warrant 
additional tightening.

BI introduced a host of measures at the 
June to September policy meetings , 
including FX monetary hedging 
instruments and a mechanism to provide 
foreign investors with greater flexibility 
in managing IDR-denominated 
investments in Indonesia.  
These included –  
a) swap hedging per tenor bucket was 
increased to 3M - 15%; 6M - 20%; 12M - 
25%, from 12.5% earlier.  
b) DNDF incentive was increased to 6M - 
25% and 12M – 30%. An increase in FX/ 
NDF swap premium incentives for longer 
tenors will lower hedging costs and

encourage longer tenor positions, in turn 
increasing longevity of these flows;  
c) Launch of the VASTRA scheme (FX 
Market Transactions for Hedging 
through Partner Banks) got underway, 
with the naming of 14 domestic partner 
banks. This facility is designed to help 
investors transact with lower underlying 
documentation requirements, tap into 
longer banking hours , and access 
onshore hedging facilities.  
d) deepen FX and money markets by 
expanding Local Currency Transactions 
(LCT) between IDR and CNY , besides a 
few other currencies.

Policymakers are likely to tap a 
combination of administrative and 
macroprudential measures rather than 
solely interest rates to defend the 
currency as well as keep inflationary

We expect the pause on rates to extend 
into 4Q26.  This call might be at risk if 
depreciation pressures on the rupiah

cycle than our baseline (of 75bp hikes).

WIDER CAD WILL BE PARTLY 
OFFSET BY POSITIVE FLOWS

Indonesia’s 1H26 current account 
deficit (CAD) widened significantly  to -
$16bn vs -$3bn in the comparable period 
a year ago. Much of this deterioration 
was led by a narrower goods trade 
balance, while  the services deficit 
widened on the seasonal travel account 
due to the Hajj period. Higher coupon 
payments weighed on the primary 
account.  This pressure is likely to persist 
in 2H as the oil & gas trade deficit 
remains wide and export performance 
has been fi rm but tracking lower than 
regional peers, likely also impacted by 
the El Nino phenomenon in key agri 
commodities. We expect full year CAD to 
be closer to 1.8-2% of GDP from -0.1% in 
2025.

Much rests on the capital flows account. 
While 1H balance of payments (BOP) also 
widened, there was palpable 
improvement in 2Q26 vs 1Q.  2Q BOP 
narrowed significantly to $0.9bn from a 
wide $9.1bn in 1Q, helped by positive 
capital account flows – primarily 
stronger portfolio investment on SRBI 
and debt inflows, and net FDI position. 
This dependency is likely to extend to 2H, 
with capital fl ows till Sep26 holding up 
on account of hedging discounts and 
moves to improve inflows. Global 
conditions, including the narrow ID -US 
yields, however, warrant attention. 
Nonetheless, full-year BOP could remain

IN SUMMARY

IDR markets have been relatively 
steady in October despite higher oil 
prices and a bid dollar , though 
sentiment remains sensitive to external 
developments and swings in global risk 
appetite. USDIDR traded within 17600 -
18000, while 10Y yield hovered around 
7.15-7.25%. A jump in the Aug goods 
trade surplus aided this respite, 
alongside foreign purchases of domestic 
debt, which have remained positive this 
month and on a  YTD basis. Insurers, the 
central bank, and retail investors have 
remained key anchors for the bond 
market. SRBI rates are off highs to sub -
7% levels but are attracting steady 
demand, likely encouraged by hedging 
discounts. An improved outlook for flows 
has helped contain spillovers from a 
wider current account deficit. This does 
not take away from the fact that the 
rupiah is amongst the worst performers 
on a year-to-date basis.

Separately, markets will also monitor 
developments in the political economy, 
institutional architecture, and formation, 
as well as the role of state -led agencies 
(e.g., DSI) and progress on the 
centralisation of decision -making. We 
expect the BI to keep on hold, however, 
pressure to tighten policy might return if 
the US Fed hikes rates well into 2027 
and the US dollar benefits from a risk-off 
environment, weighing on the currency.

Document 1331: Swing State_ Navigating Midterm Volatility (2026-10-23)

Source PDF: all report pdf/Swing State_ Navigating Midterm Volatility (2026-10-23).pdf
Report source: Unknown

### Page 1

Deutsche Bank 
Research Institute

Swing State: Navigating 
Midterm Volatility

1 
Authors 
Laura Daniels 
Deputy Associate Director of Equity  
Research

Josh Ray 
Associate Director of Equity

Matthew Barnard 
Head of US Company Research

Parag Thatte 
Strategist

Brett Ryan 
Senior US Economist

October 23, 2026 
A client-facing version of this report is available at the Deutsche Bank Research 
Portal. The following Deutsche Bank Research analysts contributed to this report: 
Brett Ryan (econ), Binky Chadha and Parag Thatte (equity strategy), Benjamin 
Soff (data centers), Daniel Knauff (software), George Hill (healthcare), Omotayo 
Okusanya (REITs), Peter Abramowitz (office REITs), Mark DeVries (consumer and 
specialty finance), Nicole DeBlase (MI/EE), Corinne Blanchard (clean tech), 
Richa Harnain (transports), and Scott Deuschle (aerospace and defense).  
With the 2026 US midterm elections approaching, we look at key investor 
debates surrounding the event and legislative priorities of the next Congress. 
Despite the uncertainty that midterms can bring, the market appears fairly 
confident on expectations for the overall results. While a surprise Republican-
majority victory in both chambers is still possible, consensus is converging 
around current polling indicating Democrats are likely to flip the seats needed for 
a House majority and may win a Senate majority. Historically, an incumbent 
president has lost seats in 20 of the last 22 midterms. Investor expectations are 
in line with this. Polymarket, for example, is currently above 90% for Democrats 
gaining control of the House and above 60% for Democrats gaining control of the 
Senate.  
With this set of expectations, key investor debates instead focus on the 
legislative agenda for hot-ticket policy issues. Namely, these hinge on AI and 
data centers, affordability (affecting healthcare, housing, and education loans), 
and economic and fiscal policy. Debates also surround possible influence of the 
new Congress on the war in Iran and, by extension, energy prices. In this report, 
we cut through the noise on what the next Congress could reasonably advance 
from these agendas, what the impact would be on affected sectors, and how to 
address market uncertainty – and perceived certainty – into the elections. 
Historically, midterm elections have proven to be a check on administration 
policies. The number of seats lost in the midterms by the incumbent party is tied 
to the president’s approval rating going into midterms, which in turn tends to 
align with consumer confidence. President Trump’s ~38% approval rating, at a 
record low for his tenure, would suggest a little over a 45-seat loss for the 
Republican Party (in the House and Senate combined). That said, polling in the 
Senate races that will determine control of the chamber largely remains within 
the margin of error, and in 2024, Trump won in at least five of the seven core toss-
up states. Thus, the Senate remains a much closer call than the House race.

### Page 2

23 October 2026 
The Theme Screen

Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. Page 2

Figure 1: Presidential Approval vs. House Seats

Source: Real Clear Politics

Figure 2: Presidential Approval vs. Consumer Confidence

Source: The Conference Board

Whatever the outcome of the  midterms, the legislative agenda will 
still face constraints from the White House. It is all but impossible for either party 
to gain a veto -proof majority  in either chamber, minimizing the likelihood of a 
large shift in fiscal or regulatory policy. The most  immediately obvious impact of 
Democrats taking the Senate would be the ability to slow or block executive 
branch appointees, including at the Federal Reserve Board of Governors or the 
Supreme Court, should any members step down before their terms end.

### Page 3

23 October 2026 
The Theme Screen

Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. Page 3

Without garnering a two-thirds majority in both chambers, Democrats lack a clear 
path to unwind the 2025 tax cuts or enact AI-related regulatory legislation – at 
least, not without President Trump’s explicit approval. With respect to the near -
term fiscal policy outlook, the most important period for investors may be the 
“lame duck” session, the period after the November 3 election and before the new 
Congress convenes on January 3. Recall that current federal government funding 
expires on December 11, and the Trump administration is asking for a nearly 60% 
increase in defense spending, the largest since the Korean War.  In addition, the 
debt limit will become binding again around the middle of next year. In short, the 
actions during the lame duck session could determine whether the new Congress 
is seated amid a government shutdown, a contentious battle over the federal 
budget, and the debt limit looming in the background.  
In terms of the market reaction to midterm  elections, the risk-reward profile has 
typically been favorable , with 21 of the last 23 midterm years  seeing positive 
returns in the fourth quarter, with an average gain of 7% in the S&P. The gains are 
notable even after adjusting for typical positive year-end seasonality.

Figure 3: S&P Returns and Midterms

Source: Bloomberg Finance LP

It w ould not be unusual for the market to go sideways as investors hedge 
potential volatility and uncertainty, as we have seen previously ahead of other 
well-telegraphed pivotal events. This has historically been followed by a rally as 
the results became clear and  uncertainty dissipated, regardless of the result 
itself. In the current context, if election polls and prediction market probabilities 
continue being lopsided, the market may not treat the election as an uncertain 
risk event going in. Uncertainty could still ramp up after, and the typical midterm 
election rally may be pushed out. It is notable that the one prominent exception 
to the midterm rallies was in 2018 , when the market sold off sharply after the 
elections as uncertainty spiked around trade war 1.0 as well as Fed policy.

### Page 4

23 October 2026 
The Theme Screen

Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. Page 4

We note that the midterm elections also coincide with the third quarter earnings 
season, during which we expect companies to deliver growth of 34%. For next 
year, we expect growth to be a still -robust 17% with risks to the upside. 
Eventually, earnings tend to be the anchor for equities and have been for several 
years despite numerous domestic political as well as geopolitical shocks. 
Across sectors, most have rallied around past midterms in keeping with the 
market, but there isn’t a consistent pattern of out - or underperformance . This 
suggests that for the initial conditions for each sector, specific policies and 
positioning played a bigger role.  For that reason, we turn to a closer analysis of 
key legislative and policy debates impacting exposed sectors.

### Page 5

23 October 2026 
The Theme Screen

Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. Page 5

AI and Data Centers  
AI and data centers have become a campaign talking point for candidates from 
both the Democratic and Republican parties. This has spurred investor questions 
on whether to expect a national regulatory framework constraining data center 
buildouts. Some of th e headlines surrounding this debate overestimate what 
Congress can  accomplish through national legislation compared with what is 
possible at a state level, particularly during a presidential administration 
supportive of AI and data center acceleration. Still, the industry is responding to 
a political backdrop that is increasingly scrutinizing AI and data centers.  
The current administration has prioritized advancing AI and digital infrastructure 
development. The White House ’s AI Action Plan , released July 2025, included a 
set of executive orders supporting the rapid buildout of AI data centers by 
reducing certain federal regulatory and permitting burdens. The administration 
did not preempt state laws on data center infrastructure development and 
federal permitting orders generally do not override state zoning and utility rules. 
In March 2026 , the White House announced the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, 
under which large data center operators would voluntarily commit to covering 
the cost to upgrade generation, transmission, substations, or other necessary 
infrastructure to service these developments.  The industry’s response to these 
proposals has been largely constructive. The Data Center Coalition  (DCC), an 
industry group representing major  hyperscalers and data center  owners and 
operators came out in support of the initial version of the Pledge, while arguing 
that large -load customers across all industries also should cover the costs to 
upgrade energy infrastructure. According to the DCC , “the data center 
industry remains committed to being responsible partners where we  operate, 
which includes  paying our full energy costs  and investing in local jobs and 
workforce development.” 
Congress voted in September 2026 to codify the principles present in the Pledge 
via the Ratepayer Protection Act. The bill, which only required states to “consider” 
these standards, passed overwhelmingly in the House (417-3), but failed to reach 
60 votes in the Senate (57 -43). Critics noted the bill stopped short of imposing 
mandatory nationwide rules. 
Looking forward, we expect a Congress that is more focused on consumer 
protection might look to codify a more stringent version of these rules, requiring 
large-load customers to bear the full incremental costs associated with 
generation, transmission, and distribution upgrades.  However, even if such a 
framework were passed into law, we believe the overall economic impact to large 
data center operators would be relatively modest, for two reasons. 
For one, the White House would maintain a veto over  bills that include language 
it views as overly burdensome towards AI infrastructure development . Two, data 
center operators  generally underwrite projects only when they have a high 
degree of confidence in securing power and, where necessary, may already be 
embedding the cost of upgrading energy infrastructure into their investment 
plans. We expect developers to be capable of passing on sustained increases in 
power infrastructure costs to their customers , which, for many 100  MW+ 
developments, are the major investment-grade hyperscalers.

### Page 6

23 October 2026 
The Theme Screen

Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. Page 6

Though data center development is receiving increasing national attention, it is 
still largely a local issue, and the most consequential elections will be at the state 
and local levels. We have seen a number of state -driven actions on data center s 
in recent months, including: 
• In July, New York State’s governor issued an executive order to establish 
a temporary moratorium on data center development  while the state 
develops a standardized framework of rules for key issues (including 
responsibilities for power and energy infrastructure upgrades; additional 
power generation; clean energy; water use, emission, and waste 
management; and state/local financ ial incentives). The New York 
legislature also passed a one -year moratorium on Department of 
Environmental Conservation permits and approvals for 20  MW+ data 
center developments. 
• In August, Texas’ governor directed the state’s public utility commission 
to conduct a comprehensive audit of every data center advancing 
through the ERCOT (Texas’s grid operator) interconnection process. The 
audit will cover several notable areas including public financial support, 
electricity demand and supply, water use, community impacts, and 
ownership and control. 
• In September, California’s governor passed a comprehensive regulatory 
package, covering electricity, water, reporting, and environmental 
review. Most of these provisions take effect January 1, 2027, and phase 
in through 2027 -2028, but the package does not ban data centers or 
impose a statewide moratorium on development activity. 
• Oregon, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and other states have also 
established orders to create standards and frameworks governing data 
center development (but without imposing broad moratoriums). 
At the more local level, a large number of moratoriums have been passed on new 
data center development. Data collected by SemiAnalysis, an independent 
research firm, shows that, as of September, more than 300 local data  center 
moratoriums have been adopted nationwide across counties, municipalities, 
townships, and other local governments.  
However, these state and local moratoriums appear  thus far to be less impactful 
to near- and medium-term development activity than headline coverage might 
otherwise suggest. According to SemiAnalysis, only about 2.3 GW of the 38 GW 
of data center capacity planned or under construction for 2027 has faced delays 
as a result of  the New York state executive order (0.8 GW) and/or local 
moratoriums (1.5 GW). 
We believe the primary reasons that moratoriums are, in reality, less likely to 
impact near -term development activity are (1) that these moratoriums largely 
impact new projects and applications (rather than existing developments in  
progress), (2) there may be flexibility to relocate or rezone early-stage projects in 
response to moratoriums, and (3) data center developers are increasingly 
partnering with local communities to gain their support via investments and other 
programs (as we wrote about recently).  Potential regulatory risk has not yet 
slowed capex spending patterns, with capex spend still expected to climb from

$0.5 trillion in 2025 to $1.3 trillion by 2027; data centers typically represent ~20-
30% of the total bill of materials for new AI capacity.  
Although the practical impact on near- and medium-term development pipelines 
appears less pronounced than headlines might suggest, all this is not to say that 
data centers will not face increasing local opposition following the midterms. 
Indeed, i n our conversations with industry participants, there is an 
acknowledgment that greater public scrutiny of data centers is not going away.  
Additional moratoriums, zoning restrictions, permitting requirements, or utility -
related conditions could affect the pace, cost , and overall feasibility of future 
projects.

Affordability Agenda: Healthcare, Housing, and 
Education Loans  
The affordability agenda has become a centerpiece of many Democratic as well 
as Republican campaign platforms.  This platform is impacting investor 
debates across healthcare, housing, and student loans. In healthcare,  the push 
among some Democrats for expanded health coverage under the Medicare for All 
banner is placing pressure on managed care stocks, but meanwhile, companies 
with exposure to Medicaid and  the Affordable Care Act (ACA) could see a 
supportive political backdrop. On housing, investor debates on the impacts of the 
affordability agenda have continued since passage of legislation in July 2026 that 
caps the number of single -family homes for -profit institutional investors can 
purchase. Affordability of higher education is likewise part of the conversatio n, 
leading investors to debate which levers Congress could pull that would affect 
student loan companies.  
Healthcare 
In healthcare, w e see the upcoming midterm elections as a sentiment event for 
managed care stocks , not a policy event.  With the presidential veto in place 
through 2028, we do not expect the government to enact direct healthcare 
legislation during the next Congress. Forecasts place the probability of a change 
in House control at roughly 79%, with both chambers changing in about 44% of 
simulations. Although investor skittishness around Medicare for All (M4A) rhetoric 
is high, we see the likelihood of M4A replacing private coverage as a near -zero 
probability in this timeframe.  
M4A has no realistic legislative path before 2029, but the rhetoric weighs on 
managed care organization (MCO) stock multiples by raising perceived long-term 
risk rather than affecting near -term earnings. Polling from  Kaiser Family 
Foundation, a health policy research organization, shows support for M4A at a 
decade-plus high, and the 2018 –2019 cycle suggests that increased campaign 
attention can pressure MCO multiples even without a direct policy impact. We 
expect similar sentiment -driven pressure through year -end and potentially into 
the 2028 primary cycle but would not view it as a change i n near -term 
fundamentals.  
For Medicare Advantage, we see a h eadline risk over earnings reality. The near-
term earnings impact for affected companies should be limited, because the US 
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has finalized a 2.48% Medicare 
Advantage (MA) rate increase for 2027, versus 0.09% in the advance notice. A 
change in House control would instead increase focus on 2028 payment policy, 
risk adj ustment, and prior authorization. Coding reform already has bipartisan 
support: sponsors estimate that the Cassidy -Merkley No UPCODE Act could 
generate up to $275  billion of savings over ten years, while MedPAC estimates 
coding intensity will add roughly $40  billion to 2025 Medicare Advantage  costs 
relative to traditional Medicare. In our view, the more immediate consideration is 
potential multiple pressure rather than a measurable change to company 
earnings.  
However, the next Congress could b enefit Medicaid funding and ACA policy. 
Medicaid and the ACA appear relatively better positioned, although any benefit

### Page 9

23 October 2026 
The Theme Screen

Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. Page 9

would likely be reflected first in sentiment and lower perceived policy risk rather 
than near -term estimate revisions. Medicaid community engagement 
requirements take effect in most states by January 1, 2027. Although repeal 
remains unlikely given the presidential veto, a change in House control could shift 
the year -end funding debate toward  restoring or  preserving federal Medicaid 
support, which could ease state budget pressure and support rate -setting. The 
ACA policy backdrop could also become more supportive, although we see 
limited scope for enhanced premium subsidies to return before 2029 after the 
three-year extension passed by the House stalled.  
Housing 
Turning to the housing sector, the likely midterm outcome of a split government 
would result in more gridlock. Historically, political gridlock in terms of passing 
new regulation has been a tailwind for the real estate sector, reducing regulatory 
risk at the federal level. In the scenario of a split Congress, in which the Democrats 
have a majority in the House but not the Senate, bills with bipartisan support have 
a greater likelihood to become law. Two key areas in which this bipartisan support 
exists are housing affordability and consumer protection. 
Among real estate investment trusts ( REITs), we see Residential as among the 
most impacted subsectors, particularly as it relates to the affordability debate. 
Regardless of the election outcome, housing affordability has become front and 
center on the political agenda  across both parties. F ederal legislation  is more 
likely to target supply -side solutions, as legislation restricting rent increases is 
typically handled at the local and state level. We think Multifamily would be the 
most likely subsector impacted, as a push to expand rental housing supply could 
lead to eased zoning restrictions, particularly in supply -constrained coastal 
markets that have historically benefited from higher barriers to entry. That said, 
this would likely take years to materialize. With a Democratic majority , Congress 
could voice opposition to the influence of large institutional landlords, but we see 
this strictly as a sentiment risk to stocks.  
Single Family For Rent (SFR) is less exposed to near -term legislative shocks, as 
the sector was a focus of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act passed in July 
2026 over the summer. The  measure impacts institutional owners’ ability to buy 
homes off the MLS but contains specific carve-out provisions that will allow them 
to keep developing build -to-rent (BTR) product and buy excess inventory from 
homebuilders, the sector's preferred acquis ition channel in recent years. The 
ROAD to Housing Act also contained provisions that could theoretically ease the 
production of manufactured homes, the main business segment for 
Manufactured Housing (MH) REITs. The first-order impact is likely more flexibility 
in home designs that could lead to further densification of MH communities, 
although we note emerging investor debate about the long -term impacts of 
increased MH production on competitive supply for a property type t hat has 
historically been supply constrained, mainly due to NIMBY-ism.  
Parallel to the conversation on affordability, it is clear that, regardless of which 
political party may be in power following the midterms, a major focus remains 
addressing the US fiscal deficit and its continued growth. We continue to pay 
attention to potential budget cuts or sequestration to slow government spending 
and reduce the deficit, which could have an impact on real estate.  Key areas to 
watch include cuts to healthcare spending (which would be a negative for skilled

nursing focused REITs, given Medicare is a major revenue source for their tenant 
base) and cuts that would impact Office REITs with large government exposure.  
We also worry that an elevated federal deficit and the elevated Treasury 
borrowing needs today create a risk that interest rates will remain  higher for 
longer. This puts pressure on real estate valuations and cost of financing for REITs 
to drive external growth via acquisitions and development. A split Congress is 
likely to result in more difficult budget negotiations and increased oversight, but 
it remains unclear w hat the ultimate outcome would be to address the budget 
deficit issue. 
With real estate being more dependent on local market dynamics, we believe the 
more likely regulatory impact would come from local regulation. This could show 
up on the ballots during the midterms , with increased possibility of rent control 
legislation targeted at residential real estate as well as self -storage, as cities and 
municipalities focus on affordability issues. There is also growing legislative 
pushback at the local level against development of real assets such as data 
centers given the large power requirements, as discussed in detail elsewhere in 
this report.  
Education Lending 
Midterm campaign platforms on education affordability  have a bearing on the 
consumer and specialty finance sector. Much of the policy exposure in this sector 
is through the executive branch bodies, not Congress, however. This includes, for 
example, regulatory authorities  such as the FDIC (Federal Deposit Insurance 
Corporation), the CFPB (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ), or the FHFA 
(Federal Housing Finance Agency, which regulates Fannie Mae and Freddie 
Mac). That said, historical data shows that student loan company stocks can still 
directionally align with midterm party outcome and expectations  in Congress, 
although the sample size is small.

Mixed Impacts of Economic and Fiscal Policy  
Democratic and Republican candidates have aimed to distinguish themselves 
from their opponents along a range of economic and fiscal policy matters, 
including tariffs, tax, labor, and the budget. In reality, the outcome of the 
midterms, regardless of which party prevails, is likely to present a mixture of relief 
and restrictions affecting businesses. In some cases, investor fears over sweeping 
economic policy changes are overblown for topics over which Congress 
realistically has limited influence, presenting more headline  risk than a risk to 
fundamentals. In considering these, we look to industrials that are particularly 
sensitive to key investor debates , spanning multi-industry/electrical equipment, 
clean tech and alternative energy, transport, and defense.  
For the multi-industry and electrical equipment (MI/EE) sector, historical midterm 
election cycles suggest a generally constructive backdrop heading into election 
day, with positive returns in six of the past seven elections. On average, the MI/EE 
group has gained ~5% during the three months preceding historical midterm 
elections and ~8% during the final month prior. Relative outperformance v ersus 
the S&P 500 has been less consistent; we observed outperformance in only four 
of seven cycles, though the group still generated average excess returns of 
~250bps over the preceding three months and ~270bps over the preceding 
month.  
Overall, the data supports a favorable absolute return backdrop ahead of 
midterms, but significant stock -level dispersion suggests company -specific 
fundamentals and factor leadership have historically mattered more than the 
election cycle alone. We mapped out election results scenarios across key policy 
pillars for our coverage (tax policy and capital investment; trade, tariffs, and 
supply chains; energy, grid, and power infrastructure; AI and data center 
regulation; and the regulatory environment). We focus on two key scenarios: one 
in which Republicans maintain control of both chambers, and a divided 
government that sees the Democrats controlling one or both chambers of the 
legislative branch.  
Under a divided government, we expect stock -level dispersion would likely 
narrow, with globally exposed companies receiving some trade policy relief and 
HVAC/automation companies benefiting from a potentially more supportive 
regulatory backdrop. However, should Republicans maintain control of Congress, 
our scenario analysis suggests this would be favorable for electrical equipment 
and power infrastructure manufacturers, due to a combination of pro-investment 
tax policy, faster infrastructure deployment, and a lighter AI regulatory 
framework. That said, globally exposed companies could face incremental tariff 
and retaliation risks.  
Looking to the clean tech and alternative energy sector, the midterm elections 
could represent a positive tailwind . T he next Congress might be positioned to 
pursue targeted extensions or modifications to certain clean -energy tax credits. 
The introduction of H.R. 8477, which proposes to restore several clean energy tax 
credits rolled back in late 2025, seems to signal tha t some, albeit a limited 
number, of Republicans could be supportive of this initiative. If the Democrats 
gain a majority in the House but not the Senate in the midterms, it is plausible that 
Democrats could find sufficient  Republican support to advance

### Page 12

23 October 2026 
The Theme Screen

Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. Page 12

legislation extending clean -energy credits, though they would still face 
significant legislative hurdles. A midterm outcome in which Republicans retain 
control of both chambers is likely to maintain the status quo  for the remaining 
existing tax credits, especially for those tied to domestic manufacturing. While 
those could potentially see further extension, we think this is a limited outcome.    
While we see a low probability of a major change in, or support for, the residential 
tax credits that expired at the end of 2025 (25D), we envision a scenario in which 
indirect residential tax credits (48E) could be extended, which would help boost 
part of the demand. Softness  in demand is expected to remain going into 2027, 
still impacted by the phaseout of the 25D tax credits, the eventual roll-off of safe-
harbor benefits, and a more constrained financing environment.  
From a manufacturing tax credit standpoint,  there could be additional tailwinds  
if we were to see any manufacturing tax credit extension or positive modification 
(although lower probability, in our view) . This would also likely improve utility -
scale project economics if broader project -related credits are preserved, though 
upcoming elections could cause a slowdown in new booking activity until 
legislative uncertainty clears.  
For Transports,  the midterms would be most relevant for the trucking supply 
thesis. Truckload stocks could have a modest negative reaction to a Democratic 
majority if investors expect some rollback of the Trump administration’s 
constraints on drivers , which has tightened supply . We would separate 
perception from fundamentals, however. The election of a Democratic Congress 
would not automatically by itself change leadership at the Department of 
Transportation (DOT) and the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration 
(FMCSA), the executive branch entities driving much of the current push  for 
restrictions on drivers.  
One possible impact of  the midterms for  Transports is if  a change in 
Congressional control  contributed to a faster resolution of the war in Iran . Any 
resulting lower energy prices would be a positive for Transports . We view this as 
a lower -probability outcome,  however, given the constraints on a divided 
government.  
With clashes over the budget likely looming, aerospace and def ense could get 
caught in the crosshairs. W hile defense spending has historically enjoyed 
bipartisan support, it has grown politicized following the war in Iran, making it 
more difficult for a split Congress to pass such a budget. The defense budget has 
experienced significant growth over the last few years, rising from $900 billion in 
FY2024 to $1 trillion in FY2026. The Trump administration would like to see this 
trend accelerate: in April 2026, the president issued a budget request that called 
for a $1.5  trillion budget for the Department of Defense in FY 2027. With a 
continuing resolution likely into year-end, the outcome of the midterm elections 
will determine whether the next Congress can pass such a budget. If Republicans 
hold the House and Senate, we think there  is a reasonable prospect of a budget 
of $1.2 trillion or more  passing into law . Defense investors would see that as a 
substantial tailwind for beaten-up defense stocks. On the other hand, this would 
be unlikely in a split Congress, in our view.  Given all this, we see the outcome of 
the upcoming midterm elections as key to determining how US defense stocks 
will perform into year end and beyond.

23 October 2026 
The Theme Screen

Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. Page 13

Taking Stock of the Known Unknowns 
Although Republicans could maintain control of both chambers,  consensus is 
converging around polls pointing to a Democratic majority in the House  and 
possibly the Senate. The perceived certainty has allowed the investor debate 
related to midterms to focus not only on who will win but how they will govern. In 
some cases, headlines are misrepresenting what a Congress constrained by the 
executive will be able to accomplish . In other areas, legislation that is expected 
to be passed will need to be taken together with offsetting factors. Whatever the 
outcome, the political backdrop will continue to influence the market and 
investor debates in the year ahead.

### Page 2

The US midterm elections take place on 3 November. All 435 seats
in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are
up for election. With Trump’s approval rating hitting a record low
according to a Fox News poll, it is no wonder that the pollsters
currently suggest the Democrats lead by around 8 percentage
points nationally. A Democratic takeover of Congress therefore
seems most likely, but a Democratic clean sweep is not certain.

We look at what the possible outcomes could mean for healthcare
and pharma.
The key differences
For healthcare, US voters face a clear choice: Democrats want to
expand Medicaid and insurance coverage, as well as permanently
extend Aﬀordable Care Act (ACA) subsidies. Republicans favour the
opposite approach, with greater responsibility shifted to individual
states.
For pharma, on the other hand, the old political divide of
"Democrats regulate, Republicans leave industry alone" is largely

gone. Both parties now see the pharma and biotech sector as key
to national security, and therefore want more domestic
manufacturing. They also both want lower drug prices. The
diﬀerence is how they get there. Democrats lean toward
government negotiation under Medicare and incentivising domestic
manufacturing through other means than tariﬀs; Republicans lean
toward most-favoured-nation (MFN) pricing and trade pressure. In
short, the policy risks diﬀer slightly depending on the outcome, but

the objectives are largely bipartisan.

on US consumers and Europe as well as

Scenario 1: Republican revival
A Republican victory will embolden President Trump to entrench his

healthcare and industrial policy legacy during his ﬁnal two years in
oﬃce. His administration would face fewer congressional obstacles
to implementing Medicaid restrictions, maintaining a more limited
federal role in insurance coverage and resisting restoration of
enhanced ACA subsidies.
For consumers as well as healthcare providers and insurers, the
main risk would be further coverage erosion. Hospitals in Medicaid-
heavy markets could see more uncompensated care.

Pharmaceutical volumes could be aﬀected where patients lose
coverage or struggle to aﬀord prescriptions.
For pharma, Republican control of Congress would give Trump
greater scope to embed MFN pricing and use tariﬀ exemptions and
company agreements to further secure US manufacturing
commitments. Pharmaceutical companies would gain greater
clarity about the direction of policy, but not relief from pricing or
supply-chain pressure. In short, this would be the scenario with the

greatest continuity in pharma policy.
Scenario 2: Trump constrained
A Democratic House could obstruct legislation, control committees
and launch investigations. But bills restoring ACA subsidies or

### Page 4

mitigating Medicaid cuts would face a Republican Senate and,
ultimately, Trump’s veto. Healthcare policy would therefore become
more confrontational but not necessarily very diﬀerent in practice.
Coverage losses and stricter Medicaid eligibility rules would remain
immediate issues, while Democrats would use hearings and must-
pass spending legislation to put pressure on the administration.
Pharma would face detailed scrutiny of MFN deals, tariﬀs, and the

implementation of Medicare negotiations. Yet neither party would
control all the levers required for sweeping reform. This could create
room for narrower bipartisan measures, particularly around
Pharmacy Beneﬁt Managers (PBM) and hospitals. Broader reform
would probably stall, meaning that not much would change for the
US consumer.
Scenario 3: Democratic clean sweep
Control of both chambers would give Democrats their strongest
platform to restore ACA subsidies, soften Medicaid cuts and make

healthcare aﬀordability a central condition in budget and defence
negotiations. This would lower premiums and out-of-pocket costs
for US consumers, while helping more people retain or gain health
insurance. Coverage expansion is also likely to improve hospital
ﬁnances and prescription volumes.
For pharma, Democrats would likely slow MFN momentum by
demanding transparency around the MFN deals as well as
challenging their design and cost. It is also likely that they would

want to prioritise expanding or accelerating the Medicare drug-price
negotiations agreed under the IRA, alongside greater scrutiny of
launch prices and PBMs.
Moreover, stronger congressional protection of National Institutes of
Health (NIH) funding, scientiﬁc institutions and Food and Drug
Administration (FDA) review capacity would support biotech and
early-stage innovation. If Democrats truly make drug-price
negotiations a priority, then this scenario could lead to a mixed

outcome: greater price pressure, but a stronger public research base
and a better-funded FDA.

### Page 5

Why a Democratic clean sweep would be
good news for European governments
For Europe, pressure on the pharma industry to localise in the US
will remain under all three scenarios. Democrats may criticise the
means, but they also view pharmaceutical supply chains as a
national-security issue. Republican and Democratic policy
objectives therefore broadly align, while Trump retains substantial
executive authority over trade.
The biggest diﬀerence is that a Democratic clean sweep would

demand greater transparency around MFN deals and increase price
pressure through Medicare negotiations. That scrutiny could raise
the chances of European governments slow-walking their own price
negotiations in the expectation that MFN terms may be delayed or
revised. By contrast, a Republican clean sweep would reinforce
policy continuity and further strengthen the pull for manufacturing
investment to move to the US.
Europe’s structural competitiveness issue therefore remains under

all scenarios, but is most pronounced if the Republicans win both
the House and the Senate. Unless Europe improves
commercialisation, capital market depth and harmonises
regulation, it risks losing both production to the US and intellectual
property/partnerships to China.
Beijing is now more likely to block licensing
deals than Washington
China will also keep facing bipartisan pressure. Both parties now
view pharma and biotech as key to national security interests and

support greater domestic manufacturing and reduced foreign
dependencies. However, China’s dominance in active
pharmaceutical ingredients is unlikely to wane any time soon.

Furthermore, commercial demand for Chinese innovation will not

disappear simply because supply-chain policy becomes more
restrictive. We still forecast Chinese outlicensing to increase to more
than $250bn this year, nearly double the deal value of 2025
despite geopolitical tensions. What's more, licensing restrictions are
now more likely to come from Beijing than Washington. The sector
has convinced US policymakers that these deals are needed to
access innovation, while China is considering restrictions on
acquisitions of biopharma platforms involving key technologies.

These deals will continue under any scenario, but especially if
Republicans retain control of Congress. If there is a Democratic
clean sweep, however, Trump will tend to focus more on foreign and
trade policy, meaning China could end up in the crosshairs. This, in
turn, could mean greater scrutiny of licensing and slower growth –
not a decline – in dealmaking in 2027.

Document 1424: ここが知りたい『投資信託販売チャネルの変化と現在地』

Source PDF: all report pdf/ここが知りたい『投資信託販売チャネルの変化と現在地』.pdf
Report source: Unknown
Date: 未知日期
Pages: 1
Status: ok

### Page 1

投資信託販売チャネルの変化と現在地

資産運用調査部　主席研究員　大木 剛（おおき つよし）
　個人の資産運用において、 投資信託はNISAによる資
産形成やリタイアメン ト資金の運用などで、 重要性を増し
ている。 投資信託の販売では、 1998年12月の銀行窓販
解禁から四半世紀以上が経過した。 ここでは、 1999年以
降の公募投資信託の販売チャネル別の純資産額 （販売 ・
解約 ・ 時価変動が反映） と構成比率の推移を資料 １ で確認
したい。
　銀行窓販の解禁から1年後の1999年末時点で、 証券
は46.4兆円 （比率90％） 、 銀行等は2.8兆円 （同5％） とな
り、 その後も銀行等は預金取引等を背景とする顧客基盤
を活かし、 2007年末には34.0兆円 （同43％） まで比率
を高めた。 一方、 証券は45.3兆円 （同57％） と比率が低
下した。
　もっ とも、 銀行等の比率は2007～2008年をピークに
低下し、 証券の比率は上昇に転じた。 証券の純資産額に
は機関投資家も保有するETF （上場投資信託） が含まれ、
2010年代以降は日本銀行による大量買入れも統計上の
証券比率を大きく押し上げた。 資料 １ ・ ２ では、 個人向け投
資信託の動きをみるためETFを除いており、 それでも
2026年8月末時点では、 証券は159.9兆円 （同70％） 、 銀
行等は67.2兆円 （同29％） となっている。
投資信託の銀行窓販は証券にどれだけ迫ったか
　2009年以降の証券の比率上昇には、 証券各社の取組
みに加え、 いくつかの要因が考えられる。
　まず、 近年はNISAなどを活用した投資信託積立の拡大
により、 資産形成層を中心に大手オンライン証券会社の
利用が大きく増えている。
　また、 メガバンク等では、 顧客層に応じたグループ内の
銀行と証券の役割分担を強化し、 銀行顧客の富裕層や資
産形成層にもニーズに応じて、 証券がサービスを提供す
る動きが寄与している。
　さらに地域銀行において、 銀行の個人向け投資信託事
業を大手証券等との包括提携の下で共同運営する動き
も、 証券比率の上昇に作用している。
　一方で、 銀行等の純資産額も近年は堅調に伸びてお
り、 比率低下は、 銀行の落ち込みによるものではなく、 証
券の伸びが上回った影響が大きい。
　もっ とも、 「銀行と証券のどちらが高成長か」 という比較
より、 顧客ニーズに応じた役割分担の重要性が増してい
る。 2026年7月に政府が策定した 「金融戦略」 も、 インベ
ス トメン トチェーンの機能強化を掲げている。 多様な資産
運用ニーズに各金融サービスの担い手が強みを活かし
て応えることが、 資産運用立国の深化につながろう。
資産運用立国の深化に求められる取組み

景気は弱い動き
中国景気は弱い動きが続いている。9月の製造業PMIは50.1と前月から上昇し、好不況の境目である50を3カ月ぶりに上
回った。構成指数をみると、生産は大きく上昇した一方、就業人員の低下が全体の改善ペースを抑制した。非製造業PMI
は50.2と3カ月ぶりに50を上回ったが、過去と比べると低水準で推移している。なお、2026年4～6月期の実質GDP成長
率は前年比＋4.3%と伸びが鈍化し、季節調整済み前期比（年率換算）も＋3.6%と政府目標の「4.5～5%」を下回った。

固定資産投資は減少、生産は底堅く推移
8月の固定資産投資（年初来累計値）は前年比－7.2%と、前月から減少幅が拡大した。情報サービス業などハイテク産
業の投資は増加したものの、不動産開発投資やインフラ投資を中心に幅広い分野で低迷している。
8月の工業生産は前年比＋5.2%と増加し、底堅く推移している。リチウムイオン電池（前年比＋57.2%）や工業用ロボット
（同＋34.6%）が大幅に増加するなど、技術集約型のハイテク製造業（同＋16.7%）が全体を牽引した。

消費は弱い動き、物価は低迷
8月の小売売上高（名目）は前年比＋0.4%と、前月から増加幅が縮小した。需要が強く、価格上昇も顕著な通信機器（前
年比＋27.3%）は大幅な増加が続いた一方、政策効果の剥落や不動産不況を背景に自動車（同－18.5%）や建築・リ
フォーム材料（同－11.8%）の減少が大きかった。なお、季節調整済み前月比は－0.13%と、3カ月ぶりにマイナスだった。
8月の消費者物価は前年比＋0.8%と、中東情勢の混乱に伴う物価押し上げ効果が和らぎ、前月に続き低い伸びとなった。

為替は元高、株価は下落
人民元の対ドルレート（9月末）は1ドル＝6.71元だった。大幅な貿易黒字に加え、米国政治・経済の先行き不透明感を背
景としたドルへの慎重な見方が根強く、ドル安・元高が進んだ。8月末の外貨準備高は3兆4,383億ドルと増加した。
9月の上海総合株価指数は下落した。月中旬まで横ばいで推移したが、月末の米中首脳会談の成果が市場の期待を下
回ったことから株価は下落し、約2カ月ぶりの安値を記録した。業種別指数は、材料やエネルギーの下落が大きかった。

9月の米中首脳会談は一定の成果も、中心は対話継続の確認
9月24日、米国・ワシントンで米中首脳会談が実施された。5月の会談で打ち出された「建設的戦略安定関係」の構築を再
確認したほか、年内あと2回の会談の可能性が示唆されるなど、首脳間の対話の継続が確認された（下図）。
具体的には、米中双方が300億ドル相当の品目で関税引き下げに合意したほか、AI分野で対話枠組みを構築する方針で
合意するなど、個別分野では一定の進展が得られた。もっとも、総じてみると内容は概ね想定内であり、米中対立の全面
的な解消には至っていない。貿易戦争の休戦も今年11月までとされた期限が2カ月延長されたにとどまっており、今後も
両者間で対話を継続することを確認したことが最大の成果だったといえよう。
2026年9月の米中首脳会談における主な内容

輸出価格は上昇も、デフレ輸出への懸念はなお強い
中国の輸出価格が足元で上昇している（左図）。2023年以降、EVや太陽光パネル、鉄鋼を中心に輸出価格は下落傾向
にあり、廉価品の輸出が海外市場を席巻する「デフレ輸出」が国際問題となったが、2026年4月以降、状況が一変した。品
目別でみると、世界的に需給が逼迫している集積回路やPC、PC部品の価格上昇が顕著である。
もっとも、足元の価格上昇は一部の品目に偏っている。HSコード4桁で分類した全1,204品目のうち、足元でも5割近くで価
格が下落している（右図）。このため、デフレ輸出への懸念は依然として根強い。

Deckers 
(DECK.O/DECK US)

美國市場疲態顯現 
重要訊息  
Deckers  2Q FY27 (財年止於 3 月；7-9 月) 財報 優於預期 ，但展望 暴露美國
消費前景趨 疲。管理層下調 FY27 營收展望 ，並表示市場庫存調整可能延伸
至 2027 年春夏季。  
評論及分析  
2Q FY27 利潤率為亮點 。2Q FY27 稅後淨利 年增 17%至 3.1 億美元，折合
每股盈餘 2.32 美元，優於市場預期 28%，主因利潤率超前， 且有美國政府
退稅 挹注每股盈餘 0.28 美元。營收年增 4%至 14.8 億美元 ，略低於指引，
係受歐洲第三方物流  (3PL) 轉型導致運輸延誤及部分電商業務疲軟影響。
排除一次性退稅利益，全價銷售、 產品組合優化及 費用控管帶動毛利率及
營利率分別年增、季增至 57.4% 、23.2% ，高於市場預估 。 
美國市場 壓力 漸增 。管理層觀察到美國消費者採購行為轉變，客流量集中
促銷活動期間， 並有延後購買現 象。加上運動鞋領域同業促銷競爭加劇，
公司 堅守價格底線 導致直接面對消費者銷售成長明顯趨緩， 2Q FY27 美國
銷售 再度陷入年減 0.4%。作為應對策略，管理層計畫強化 高端產品在歐美
批發分銷管道布局，預計 2027 年春季至秋季 120 美元以上價格帶產品將
擴大市佔率，但價位低於 120 美元 的產品可能因競爭激烈而表現較疲軟 。 
營收展望 調降。公司下調 FY27 營收展望至年增 4-5% ( 前次為 7-8%)，反
映 Hoka 和 UGG 貢獻分別下修至高、低個位數成長 ，而歐洲 物流延誤需求
將無法完全補上；不過， IEEPA 退稅 仍支撐 FY27 毛利率及營利率財測分別
上調至 58.5% 、23.0% 。短期而言，預計 3Q FY27 營收年增低個位數，遜
於市場預期之高個位數成長 。 未來將 保持庫存緊縮 策略， 並專注全價銷售。 
投資建議  
我們預估 Deckers FY26-28 獲利年複合成長率大幅趨緩至僅 4% (F Y20-26
為 24%) 將壓抑股價動能 ；維持「持有」評等，目標價下調 至 86.6 美元，
基於 FY27-28 平均每股盈餘預估 11 倍，對比歷史本益比區間為 10-35 倍。 
投資風險  
上檔風險為消費較預期強勁及品牌人氣提升。

Deckers  10 月 23 日法說會重點摘要  
 2Q FY27 稅後淨 利年增 17%至 3.1 億 美 元，折合 每股盈餘 2.32 美 元，
優於市場預期 28%， 主因利潤率超前，及美國政府退稅貢獻 每股盈餘
0.28 美元。由於歐洲第三方物流  (3PL) 轉型導致 的運輸延誤 以及部分
電商業務疲軟， 本季 營收低於指引 ，年增 4%、季增 45%至 14.8 億
美元。排除一次性 退稅利 益，毛利率仍年增 1.2、季增 0.9 個百分點
至 57.4% ，主要得益自 全價銷售 及產品組合優化 ；再加上費用控管，
營利率 23.2% 優於市場共識之 20.3%。 
 市場 別營收：美國  (佔總營收 57%) 再度轉弱至年 減 0.4% ，主要受
運動鞋領域促銷活動增加之 影響 ，公司並未參與削價競爭 。國際市場 
(43%) 年增 9%，亞太地區為主要成長來源 ，而歐洲 第三方物流運輸
延誤 造成的負面影響約 2,200 萬美元。  
 品牌別營收： Hoka ( 佔總營收 46%) 年增 7%，批發業務與 DTC 銷售
分別年增 9% (升溫)、 4% (快速 冷卻 ，反映美國市場面臨壓力 )。UGG 
(53%) 年增 4%，批發業務年增 7%，抵銷 DTC 通路 8%衰退。其他
品牌  (1%) 則年減 54%。 
 產品別表現： 核心產品系列銷售 良好，其中以 Bondi 系列最為突出，
Clifton Pro 亦廣受好評。然而，消費者和批發合作夥伴的回饋表明，
今年有部分產品更新效果不如預 期，未來數季將進行一些改善工作。  
 通路別營收：批發業務  (佔總營收 74%) 年增加速至 6%，直接面對
消費者  (DTC ，26%) 則陷入年減 2%。 
 2Q FY27 庫存週轉天數 年增 6%、但季減 2%至 128 天， 仍低於過去
十年同期平均水準之 147 天。公司計畫保持庫存緊縮，並專注於全價
銷售。 
 管理層下調 FY27 營收展望至年增 4-5% (前次為 7-8%)；Hoka 和 UGG
貢獻分別下修至年增 高、低個 位 數。然而，考量 IEEPA 退稅挹注 ，FY27
毛利率及營利率財測則分別上調至 58.5% 、23.0%。加計 FY27 股票
回購 10 億美元，現估 稀釋後每股盈餘落在 7.80-7.95 美元。 
 若不計入 IEEPA 退稅挹注， 公司 預計 FY27 毛利率及營利率 分別約 為
57.0 %、略高於 21.5% ，大致符合市場預期。  
 短期而言，預計 3Q FY27 營收將 年增低個位數， 低於市場預期 ；品牌
別方面， Hoka 、UGG 將分別年增低中、 低個位數。 3Q FY27 稀釋後
每股盈餘預估落在 3.52-3.60 美元 (加計 IEEPA 退稅挹注 0.24 美元) 。 
 Mach 8 已於秋季初上市 ，為迄今為止 Mach 系列中表現最好的一款。
預計 2027 年 1 月推出 Bondi 10 和 Fly Pace，4 月 Mach Pro 接續亮相 。
6 月將 進一步 發售 Bondi Ultra X ，售價 325 美元/雙，其三密度 eTPU
中底提升緩震性能 至全新高度，標誌著 HOKA 創新技術的 重大躍進 。 
 UGG 銷售高峰集中在 11 月底至 12 月初。去年市場環境良好且 天氣
宜人 ，銷售季表現非常強勁，帶動 12 月及 1 月訂單追加； 預計今年
補貨量不會達到去年水準。 
 管理層觀察到消費者行為的 兩大轉變： (1) 消費者越來越追求折扣，

### Page 3

美國 Deckers

十月 27, 2026 研究網站: https://investment.kgisia.com.tw/Portal/Report/Index/Zh/R  3

客流量集中在促銷活動期間 ；及 (2) 消費者購買商品更 注重 目的性，
優先考慮 「即買即穿」 和具實用 性的產品 ，甚至等到接近實際需求時
才會購買 (延後購買 )。 
 美國市場感受到較大 壓力。目前消費者會盡可能透過線上批發商購買
產品 ，而這些批發商促銷力道非常 大。公司不願陷入這種過度促銷的
氛圍，因此美國 DTC 銷售成長將低於批發業務。  
 2027 年春季 至秋季，公司將持續 強化美國和歐洲批發分銷管道布局 ，
尤其價位在 120 美元以上的產品可望擴大市佔率， 但價位區間低於
120 美元的產品可能因競爭激烈 而流失市佔率 。 
 截至 2Q FY27 止，公司已回購股票 6.37 億美元，佔已發行 股數 5%，
遠超年初預期；而 剩餘授權額度約 44 億美元。

ESG 圖表定義  
項目 定義 說明 
能源使用 
直接與間接能源消耗總量(十億焦耳) 
- 公司運營範圍內消耗之能源總量 
- 能源使用總量 = 直接能源消耗總量 + 間接能源消耗量 
- 總能源使用量包括購買的能源、生產的能源 
- 就公用事業而言，輸電/電網損耗為其業務活動之一部分，被視為總能源消耗，數據不包括
為滿足能源使用而生產的電力(公用事業為出售而生產) 
- 就公用事業而言，用於能源生產的煤、天然氣或核能等原料不屬於「總能源使用」項下

購買之再生能源 
Primary 再生能源購買總量(十億焦耳) 
- 公司各種來源之能源消耗量與購買的能源中屬於自然界可再生者(太陽能、風能、水能、生
物質能、地熱能)之量 
- 如無證據顯示再生能源由公司生產，則所報告的能源數據視為購買的再生能源

再生能源使用率 再生能源占總能源消耗量之比例  
CO2 約當排放量 
直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量(公噸) 
- 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量(範圍 1 排放量) 
- 相關氣體：二氧化碳(CO2)、甲烷(CH4)、一氧化二氮(N2O)、氫氟碳化物(HFCS)、全氟化合
物(PFCS)、六氟化硫(SF6)、三氟化氮(NF3)

CO2 約當排放量營收比 
直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量(公噸)銷售(百萬元)比 
- 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量(範圍 1 排放量) 
- 相關氣體：二氧化碳(CO2)、甲烷(CH4)、一氧化二氮(N2O)、氫氟碳化物(HFCS)、全氟化合
物(PFCS)、六氟化硫(SF6)、三氟化氮(NF3)

廢棄物總量 
廢棄物總量(公噸) 
- 總廢棄物 = 無害廢棄物 + 有害廢棄物 
- 僅考慮固體廢棄物，但如液體廢棄物以公噸為單位呈報，則會將其加入求得包含液體廢棄
物之總量 
- 對於採礦、石油與天然氣等行業，tailings、廢石、煤、飛灰等廢棄物亦考慮在內

廢棄物回收率 
公司呈報的廢棄物回收率 
- 廢棄物回收率 = 廢棄物回收量/總廢棄物*100 
- 廢棄物轉化為能源或經由廢棄物焚燒產生能源視為廢棄物回收 
- 經由堆肥回收的廢棄物視為回收之廢棄物

總取水量 
總取水量(立方公尺) 
- 由呈報組織直接或經水公司等中介機構從任何水源抽取的總水量 
- 水井、城鎮/公用事業/市政用水、河水、地表水等不同之水源均予以考慮

環保支出 
環保支出總金額 
- 所有用於環境保護，或防止、減少、控制環境因素、影響、危害的投資與支出，亦包括處
置、處理、衛生、清理支出

員工流動率 
員工流動率 
- 包括任何原因(自願或非自願)離開公司的員工，如辭職、退休、自然離職/死亡、醫療失能、
冗員、裁員、重組、解僱、裁減或定期合約到期 
- 員工流動率 = (離開之員工/平均員工人數)*100 
- 平均員工人數 = (本年末員工人數 + 去年末員工人數)/2 
- 本財年末員工數 = 上個財年末員工數 + 新員工數 - 離開之員工數

女性經理 
女性經理百分比 
- 女性經理占公司經理的百分比 
- 如有不同階層之百分比，如最高階、高階、中階、初階，則會考慮中階女性經理之百分比 
- 女性經理百分比 = 女性經理人數/經理總數*100

女性員工 
女性員工百分比 
- 女性員工占公司員工總數的百分比 
- 女性員工百分比 = 女性人數/員工總數*100

教育訓練總時數 
所有員工教育訓練總時數 
- 僅考慮員工教育訓練時數 
- 包括一般員工所有類型的教育訓練(如健康與安全、環境、急難事件救援、技能與職業發展) 
- 如果數據以天為單位，則乘以 8，係假設 1 天 = 8 小時工作

每位員工教育訓練時數 平均每年每位員工總教育訓練時數  
資料來源：Refinitiv，凱基

◆現状：100ドルを挟んで乱高下

100ドル台後半に上昇。米国とイランの間で攻撃の
応酬が続いたことが背景。加えて、イエメンの武装組
織フーシがバブ・エル・マンデブ海峡付近の港湾都市
を掌握したことや 、サウジアラビアの東西パイプライン
が攻撃を受けて操業を停止したことで 、ホルムズ海
峡を迂回するルートからの石油輸出が停滞するとの
懸念も価格を押し上げ。月末にかけては、一時80ド
ル台後半に下落 。米国とイランの外交交渉が進展
するとの期待や 、東西パイプラインの輸送能力が早
期に回復するとの報道を材料に、中東からの石油供
給の増加が意識されたことが背景。
10月入り後は、90ドル前後で方向感に欠ける展
開。米国の中東への増派が価格を押し上げた一方 、
Ｇ７による石油備蓄放出の合意が価格を下押し。

### Page 4

原油
(株)日本総合研究所 原油市場展望 2026年10月3
◆長期化するホルムズ海峡の「封鎖」
足元では、米国とイランの戦闘終結に向けた交渉
が難航しており、ホルムズ海峡の封鎖が継続 。船舶
の位置情報を知らせるＡＩＳのデータに基づく推計
では、同海峡を通航するタンカーの数がほぼゼロに。
◆通常航行が停止しても、原油輸出は増加
もっとも、中東の原油輸出量は足元にかけて緩や
かに増加。海峡封鎖が続くなかでも輸出が回復して
いる背景として、次の２点が指摘可能。
第１に、迂回ルートの活用。サウジアラビアやアラブ
首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）は、パイプラインを経由して
原油を海峡外のヤンブー港やフジャイラ港に輸送 。
３月以降、これらの港からの輸出が増加。
第２に、タンカー同士の積み替え（ＳＴＳ）の活
用。報道などによると 、ＡＩＳを切って海峡を通過
することで、原油を海峡外に運び出す船舶が存在。
こうした船舶から別の船舶に積み替えられたうえで 、
原油が輸出されている模様 。実際、大規模な迂回
ルートを持たないイラク・クウェートからの輸出や、フー

シの台頭でヤンブー港からの輸出が急減しているサウ
ジアラビアの輸出が、足元にかけて増加。
◆米国・イランの戦闘激化なら、輸出減少も
先行きも、中東の原油輸出は緩やかに回復する
見通し。ただし、輸出回復は限られたパイプラインや
ＡＩＳを停止した船舶による不安定な輸送に依存。
戦闘が激化し、こうした輸送手段が 攻撃されれば、
輸出が再び減少するリスク。

予想インフレ率は日本銀行の説明する「基調的インフレ率」の一角である。日本銀行（2026）は
基調的な物価上昇率を把握する手法として、 ①変動の大きい品目の除去、 ②中長期の予想物価上昇
率を捉える、③経済モデルによる推定、の３種類のアプローチを示している。本稿推定値は②に相
当するものだ。 
①については、弊著「都区部版・消費者物価のコア指標（2026/9）～全指標が加速～」（2026 年
10 月 2 日）でその動向をまとめている。ここで試算している指標はいずれも上昇率を高めており、
中東情勢由来のコスト上昇の価格転嫁が進展していることを示唆している。3 ヶ月前時点では①の
上昇が限られる一方で、本稿試算の②の加速が目立つ状況だったが、７−９月期は逆に 価格転嫁が
進む①が強く、②に一服感が生じる形となった。①・②の双方の加速が見られれば利上げに対する
切迫感が増すことになっていたと考えられる。10 月の連続利上げも取り沙汰されているが、 今回の
期待インフレ率一服は日銀に「急がない理由」を与えるだろう。

（参考文献）

長田・中澤 （2024） 「期間構造や予測力からみたインフレ予想指標の有用性」 日銀レビュー 2024-J-
5 
西野・山本・北原・永幡 （2016） 「 『量的・ 質的金融緩和』 の3 年間における予想物価上昇率の変化」
日銀レビュー 2016-J-17 
大柴 （2024） 「インフレ予想の統計的推定の展開①～合成予想物価上昇率の有用性～」 第一生命経済
研究所 Economic Trends

3Q26 營收 略低於 預期 ，毛利率 預期 受原物料成本 呈現下滑 ：公司 3Q26
營收 12. 62 億(QoQ -2.81% ，YoY+ 12.96 %)，略 低於我們 預期， 預估 毛
利率 為 26.14% %(QoQ -3.84 ppts，YoY -2.05 ppts) ，主要受到上游磊晶及
金價持續處於高檔影響，呈現季下滑 ，預估 3Q26 EPS 為 1.07 元。公
司 3Q26 稼動率為 70%~75% ，下一季度將維持相同稼動率水準，預估
4Q26 營收為 12.63 億(QoQ+0.15% ，YoY+0.85%) ， 此外 ， 公司已於3Q26
與大部分客戶商議產品漲價，產品售價調漲將於 4Q26 生效，毛利率
預期將小幅度回升至 27.83%(QoQ+1.69ppts ，YoY -2.64ppts) 。 
2H26 營運仍 可維持高檔水準 ，持續受惠客戶提升份額 ：展望 手機 PA
因韓系手機持續擴大採用中國供應商，陸系品牌拉貨穩定，且因公司
客戶重心已轉向中高階手機，有效降低記憶體漲價對低階手機市場的
衝擊 。 公司也持續受惠於美系 IDM 廠退出中國市場及中高階手機拉貨
潮，帶動手機 PA 出貨量與 ASP 成長。 Wi-Fi 業務方面， Wi-Fi 7 滲透
率增加帶動 PA 需求，但傳統 Wi-Fi 5/6 部分 市場被矽鍺取代，展望
Router 需求為持平至小幅成長，而手機 Wi-Fi 則因大陸客戶逐漸取代
美系 IDM 廠而成長。 無人機 Wifi PA 因傳輸距離增加及高解析度圖片
回傳需求，客戶持續規格更新及提升需求量，公司現無人機客戶由過
往 1~2 家增加至 4~5 家，成長顯著。  
GaAs 及 InP PD 有望成為第二成長動能， 預期於 2028 年量產 ：公司
在 2026 年 8 月通過 28 億元資本支出 ， 用於擴建無塵室及優化生產線 ，
建立 InP 相關產品製程，預估無塵室於 2027 年底擴建完成。 光通訊業
務方面， 公司 除應用於 Datacom 短距傳輸 VCSE L 外，佈局 GaAs 及
InP PD ，並已與 多位 客戶進行開發與測試 。GaAs PD 進展較為快速，
預估最快將於 2027 年底至 2028 年初進入量產 ，而InP PD 進度較 GaAs 
PD 晚約半年，約於 2028 年年中量產。  
公司 過往 營收有 7-8 成來自手機 PA，在 PA 客戶持續提升份額、無人
機及非射頻相關應用持續顯著成長外，光通訊業務除 VCSEL 外， PD
有望在 2028 年貢獻營收，成為除手機 PA 外下一個主要成長動能。我
們預估 2026 、2027 年 EPS 分別為 5.17 、5.33 元，維持前次報告 本益
比倍數 ，基於 2027 年預估 EPS x 32 倍本益比，目標價為 171 元， 調
升評等至買進 之投資評等建議。 風險因子 ：手機 市場需求不佳 、非射
頻營收不如預期 。

に転じた。酷暑によるさまざまな調整圧力や政情不安（特にフランス）が景気の重荷になっているもよう。

Document 1626: 瑞银再度下调韩股目标位！汇率与盈利预期承压，2027年有望复苏

Source PDF: all report pdf/瑞银再度下调韩股目标位！汇率与盈利预期承压，2027年有望复苏.pdf
Report source: Unknown
Date: 未知日期
Pages: 4
Status: ok

### Page 1

瑞银年内⼆度下调韩国 KOSPI ⽬标价，从 8000 点压低⾄ 7500 点。韩元升值 15% 叠加 EPS
持续下修，外资 10 ⽉净卖出逾 190 亿韩元构成主要抛压。但瑞银强调，这是汇率驱动的 " 盈
利重置 " ⽽⾮下⾏周期，看好 2027 年复苏，上⾏⽬标剑指 9300 点。
摘要：
继今年 9 ⽉下调之后，瑞银再度下调对韩国股市的 12 个⽉⽬标位，将 KOSPI ⽬标价由此前的
8000 点下调 6% ⾄ 7500 点，对应远期市盈率 6 倍这是的⼜⼀次调整。
据追⻛交易台，瑞银在 10 ⽉ 29 ⽇报告中指出，此次下调的核⼼驱动⼒在于汇率与⾃下⽽上的盈
利修正，宏观经济压⼒⽇益加剧将拖累每股盈利，同时⽬前股市尚未充分反映韩元升值的完整
冲击，
近期 KOSPI 已从⾼点回落约 10% ，逼近其下⾏价值区间 5000 点（对应 4 倍市盈率）， KOSPI 200
看跌 / 看涨⽐率触及负⼀个标准差，历史上这⼀信号往往预⽰市场超卖。瑞银认为，当前市场⻛
险厌恶情绪已过度，在不出现持续盈利下⾏或外⽣冲击的前提下，进⼀步下⾏空间有限。

展望后市，瑞银预计 KOSPI 在年底前仍将承压，但看好 2027 年的复苏空间，⽀撑因素包括强劲
的每股盈利（ EPS ）增⻓、股东回报改善、流动性约束缓解以及加息周期趋于尾声。瑞银将上
⾏⽬标位设定为 9,300 点（对应 8 倍市盈率）。
汇率与盈利双重夹击
瑞银对 KOSPI 的⽬标位调整已是今年第⼆次。今年 9 ⽉ 18 ⽇，瑞银分析师 Yong-Suk Son 将
KOSPI 12 个⽉⽬标价从 8,800 点下调⾄ 8,000 点，降幅近 10% ，理由是利率上⾏、韩元⾛强及油
价攀升带来的宏观逆⻛。彼时，瑞银指出 10 年期国债收益率已从年初的 3.4% 跳升⾄ 4.5% ，韩国
央⾏⾃ 7 ⽉以来两度加息，油价亦突破每桶 100 美元。
时隔约六周，瑞银再度出⼿，将⽬标位进⼀步压低⾄ 7,500 点。此次下调的核⼼驱动⼒在于汇率
与⾃下⽽上的 EPS 修正。瑞银分析显⽰，韩元⾃ 6 ⽉以来升值约 15% ，若其他条件不变，将拖累
2026 年和 2027 年 KOSPI 每股盈利分别约 2% 和 10%。与此同时， 10 ⽉份市场共识 EPS ⽉度修正

幅度仅为 -0.5% ，尚未充分反映韩元升值的完整冲击，意味着后续仍存在进⼀步下修压⼒。
⾸⻚ 资讯 快讯 ⾏情 ⽇历 APP VIP 会员 ⼤师课 ⻅闻历 搜索

### Page 2

从⾏业层⾯看，化⼯、娱乐、国防、汽⻋、可选消费、多元⾦融、互联⽹及化妆品板块在 2026
年和 2027 年预期中均遭遇最⼤幅度的盈利下调；能源、运输、建筑及保险板块则相对获得上
调。
外资持续净卖出，市场情绪触及极端
资⾦流向数据揭⽰了近期市场承压的另⼀⾯。 10 ⽉以来，外资净卖出规模⾼达 190.0 亿韩元，成
为市场最主要的抛压来源，部分由企业回购（ 99.0 亿韩元）、散⼾（ 58.0 亿韩元）及本地机构
（ 32.0 亿韩元）承接。
不过，瑞银指出资⾦⾯已出现边际改善迹象：外资净卖出规模近期有所收窄，本周甚⾄转为净
买⼊；散⼾在过去两周转为净卖出，⽽企业回购在 SK 海⼒⼠（ SK Hynix ）重启回购计划后有望
获得⽀撑；养⽼⾦虽仍处于观望，但若 KOSPI 进⼀步接近下⾏价值区间，其资产配置⽬标或将
触发⼊场。
从估值与情绪指标来看， KOSPI 当前以 1.1 倍 NTM 市净率交易，与历史均值基本持平，股息收益
率达 2.7% （处于历史均值正⼀个标准差），提供⼀定估值⽀撑。剔除三星电⼦和 SK 海⼒⼠后，
KOSPI 的 NTM 市净率仅为 0.9 倍（负 0.6 个标准差）， NTM 市盈率为 6.6 倍（负 2.6 个标准差），估
值已处于历史偏低⽔平。
盈利重置⽽⾮下⾏周期， 2027 年复苏可期
尽管短期承压，瑞银对韩国股市的中期前景维持相对乐观。瑞银预测 2026 年 KOSPI 每股盈利增
速为 +258% （市场共识为 +278% ）， 2027 年为 +33% （市场共识为 +38% ），其预测已将汇率压⼒
纳⼊考量，较市场共识更为保守。
瑞银强调，当前的 EPS 下调更多是汇率驱动的 " 重置 " ，⽽⾮盈利持续下⾏周期的开端。科技板块
仍是 2026 年盈利增⻓的最⼤贡献来源， 2027 年电池材料、公⽤事业及化⼯板块有望接棒领涨。

景気は底堅い
（出所）米商務省 （出所）米供給管理協会
米国経済は堅調に推移している。4-6月期の実質GDP成長率は前期比年率2.2%に鈍化した。政府支出と在庫投資が減
少し成長率を押し下げたが、個人消費、設備投資は底堅く推移し、民間最終需要はおよそ3年ぶりの高い伸びを記録した。
企業の景況感を示すISM景況指数は、製造業、非製造業いずれも判断の目安となる50の水準を上回った。先行き、堅調
な個人消費やAI需要の一段の高まりなどから景気は底堅く推移する見込みである。
